facts.text: Flatiron Building was designated a New York City landmark in 1966, added to NRHP 1979, and became a National Historic Landmark in 1989.
The building’s nickname “Flatiron” comes from its sharp, iron‑shaped silhouette designed by Daniel Burnham, resembling a cast‑iron clothes iron.
The Flatiron’s unique triangular footprint created a natural stage at the 23rd‑Street intersection, making it one of the city’s first great skyscrapers.
Originally 20 stories tall, the Flatiron added a low “cowcatcher” retail space and a penthouse shortly after opening, expanding its usable space.
In 2014, Lego released an Architecture model of the Flatiron Building, celebrating its status as a New York landmark.
The building’s 18th and 19th‑story terraces were enclosed in the 20th century, altering its original open‑air design.
